ai.description: The Andaman Keelback reaches 60–80 cm. It is olive-brown with a yellow-white belly and a distinct dark stripe behind each eye. It features keeled scales and a characteristic yellow nuchal collar.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Andaman Keelback is best distinguished by the distinctive, bright yellow or orange-red collar on its neck, which is absent in other similar Indian keelback species.
ai.habitat: The Andaman Keelback inhabits freshwater bodies, including ponds, marshes, and paddy fields, within the tropical forests of the Andaman Islands at low elevations.
ai.behavior: The Andaman Keelback is primarily diurnal and semi-aquatic, frequently foraging in freshwater streams and marshes for small fish and amphibians.
ai.reproductionNotes: Fowlea tytleri is oviparous, typically laying clutches of 5–12 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, generally between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Andaman Keelback is endemic to the Andaman Islands in the Bay of Bengal, occurring from sea level to low elevations within this tropical island archipelago.
